mission: Discriminate why retained priors transfer, partially transfer, or fail to improve outcomes across materially different Ordivon cases.
questionOrHypothesis: Is transfer dominated by abstraction level, domain similarity, determinism/action specificity, or local observable causal credit?
evidenceSelection: P3 Game, P4 Security, P5 Web, Agent-first research/promotion method, and at least one ACS owner-surface control with exact retained evidence.
strongBaseline: T0 more abstract priors transfer better
T1 source-target domain similarity drives transfer
T2 deterministic enforceability/action specificity drives transfer
minimalCandidateOrNoChange: T-CREDIT predicts transfer from observable intermediate effects, evaluator alignment, causal distance/latency, exact escape hatch and whether the retained representation encodes a procedure/mechanism rather than a desired answer.
independentOracle: Owner-native later outcome / exact consumer-selection evidence already retained by the source experiments.
developmentSplit: P3/P5 contrasting pair plus Agent-first method.
holdoutSplit: P4 Security plus ACS owner surface(s).
invalidityConditions: transfer rating is based on prose similarity
human preference is inferred from render evidence
behavior change is counted as objective transfer
partial transfer is rounded to success
authorityBoundary: Read-only cross-owner evidence; no owner mutation.
budget: Existing evidence first. Provider follow-up only if the case court leaves competing models tied.
stopRule: Stop after each model makes an explicit prediction for every frozen case and at least one residual is preserved.
deletionOrNoChangeOutcome: If no model separates the cases, retain only case-specific laws and do not generalize transfer mechanics.
publicationBoundary: Computing-local until a prospective transfer experiment validates the leading mechanism.
